children.translated_text: The foremost and most excellent among speakers,
the lion of debaters, unconquered.
The all-seeing one, the joyful one,
the garland of radiance, the beautiful to behold,
<s>Śrīvatsa</s>, of excellent brilliance, luminous,
with rays of light and dazzling hands of splendor.
The supreme great physician, the best,
the remover of thorns (suffering), unsurpassed,
the tree of all medicines,
the great enemy of the disease of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions).
The ornament of the three worlds, the beloved one,
the glorious one, the circle of stars,
extending to the sky of the ten directions,
of great height like the banner of <s>Dharma</s>.
The one vast umbrella of the world,
the circle of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion),
the glorious lord of the lotus-dance,
the jewel-umbrella, the great sovereign.
The great king of all <s>Buddhas</s>,
bearing the essential nature of all <s>Buddhas</s>,
the great <s>yoga</s> of all <s>Buddhas</s>,
the single teaching of all <s>Buddhas</s>.
The glory of the <s>vajra</s>-jewel consecration,
the lord and master of all jewels,
the lord of all world-rulers,
the sovereign of all <s>vajra</s>-holders.
The great mind of all <s>Buddhas</s>,
the mental course of all <s>Buddhas</s>,
the great body of all <s>Buddhas</s>,
the <s>Sarasvatī</s> (eloquence) of all <s>Buddhas</s>.
The <s>vajra</s>-sun, the great light,
the <s>vajra</s>-moon of stainless radiance,
the great passion born from passionlessness,
blazing with the splendor of universal colors.
The <s>vajra</s> cross-legged seat of the perfectly awakened one,
bearing the <s>Dharma</s> proclaimed in the <s>Buddha</s>-assembly,
the glorious one born from the <s>Buddha</s>-lotus,
bearing the treasury of the knowledge of the omniscient.
The king who holds the illusion of the universe,
the great holder of the <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge,
the <s>vajra</s>-sharp one, the great sword,
the pure one, the supreme imperishable syllable.
The great vehicle that cuts through suffering,
the great weapon of the <s>vajra</s>-<s>Dharma</s>,
the conqueror of conquerors, of <s>vajra</s> profundity,
of <s>vajra</s> intellect, the knower of things as they are.
The fulfiller of all <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections),
the ornament of all <s>bhūmis</s> (stages),
the selflessness of the purified <s>Dharma</s>,
with the heart-light of the moon of perfect knowledge.
The great enterprise of the net of <s>māyā</s> (illusion),
the supreme lord of all <s>tantras</s>,
the complete <s>vajra</s> cross-legged seat,
bearing the body of exhaustive knowledge.
<s>Samantabhadra</s>, of good intellect,
<s>Kṣitigarbha</s>, the support of the world,
the great womb of all <s>Buddhas</s>,
bearing the wheel of universal creation.
Supreme in the own-nature of all existences,
perceiving the own-nature of all existences,
of the nature of non-arising, of universal purpose,
bearing the own-nature of all <s>dharmas</s>.
Of great wisdom in a single moment,
bearing the awakening to all <s>dharmas</s>,
the realization of all <s>dharmas</s>,
the sage of the ultimate reality, of foremost intellect.
Serene, of supremely clear nature,
bearing the <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) of the perfectly awakened one,
directly perceivable by all <s>Buddhas</s>,
the flame of knowledge, supremely radiant.

body.translated_text: Thus end the forty-two verses on the knowledge of discernment.

children.translated_text: The supreme accomplisher of desired aims,
the purifier of all lower realms,
the supreme being among all sentient beings, the protector,
the liberator of all sentient beings.
The sole hero in the battle against <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions),
the destroyer of the pride of the enemy of ignorance,
the intellect, the bearer of the amorous sentiment, the glorious one,
bearing the forms of the heroic and the terrible.
Swinging hundreds of arm-clubs,
dancing with foot-stamps,
the glorious one with the expanse of a hundred arms,
dancing in the expanse of the sky.
Standing on the surface of the great earth
trampled by the sole of one foot,
standing on the toenail
that has trampled the summit of the <s>Brahmāṇḍa</s> (cosmic egg).
Of single meaning, whose meaning is the non-dual <s>Dharma</s>,
the ultimate truth, the imperishable,
whose meaning is the forms of diverse perceptions,
the continuum of mind and consciousness.
Delighting in the meaning of all existences,
delighting in <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), of foremost intellect,
transcending attachment to existence and the rest,
the great delight in the three states of existence.
Pure, white as a bright cloud,
of excellent radiance like the rays of the autumn moon,
with the hue of the orb of the young sun,
with the splendor of nails of great passion.
With hair-tips of excellent sapphire blue,
bearing the tips of great blue locks,
the glory of the rays of great jewels,
the ornament of the <s>Buddha's</s> <s>nirvāṇa</s>.
Shaking a hundred world-realms,
of great stride through the <s>ṛddhipāda</s> (bases of supernatural power),
bearing great <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness), true,
the king of the four <s>smṛtyupasthāna</s> (foundations of mindfulness) <s>samādhis</s>.
Fragrant with the blossoms of the <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening),
the ocean of the qualities of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>,
the knower of the method of the <s>Aṣṭāṅgamārga</s> (Eightfold Path),
the knower of the path of the perfectly awakened ones.
Greatly attached to all sentient beings,
yet unattached, like the sky,
born from the minds of all sentient beings,
swift as the minds of all sentient beings.
The knower of the faculties and aims of all sentient beings,
the captivator of the minds of all sentient beings,
the knower of the truth of the meaning of the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates),
bearing the purity of the five <s>skandhas</s>.
Abiding at the summit of all modes of liberation,
skilled in all modes of liberation,
standing on the path of all modes of liberation,
the teacher of all modes of liberation.
One who has uprooted the twelve limbs of existence,
bearing the purity of the twelve aspects,
of the form of the method of the Four Noble Truths,
bearing the awakening to the eight knowledges.
Whose meaning is the truth of the twelve aspects,
the knower of the reality of the sixteen aspects,
the awakening of the twenty aspects,
the awakened one, the knower of all, the supreme.
The illuminator of immeasurable <s>Buddha</s>-emanations,
of myriads of bodies,
the realization in every moment,
the knower of the meaning of every moment of mind.
The illuminator of the world's purpose through the means
and methods of various vehicles,
having emerged through the three vehicles,
established in the fruit of the single vehicle.
Of a nature purified from the realm of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions),
the destroyer of the realm of <s>karma</s>,
having crossed the ocean of the flood,
having emerged from the wilderness of <s>yoga</s>.
Having well abandoned the afflictions, secondary afflictions, and defilements
together with their latent impressions,
through <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), <s>upāya</s> (skillful means), and great <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion),
the unfailing accomplisher of the world's purpose.
Whose meaning is the abandonment of all notions,
whose meaning is consciousness, the maker of cessation,
the object of the minds of all sentient beings,
the mental course of all sentient beings.
Abiding within the minds of all sentient beings,
having attained equality with their minds,
the delighter of the minds of all sentient beings,
the delight of the minds of all sentient beings.
The established conclusion, free from error,
devoid of all delusion,
of undoubting intellect, of threefold meaning,
of all meanings, of the nature of the three qualities.
Whose meaning is the five <s>skandhas</s>, of the three times,
the illuminator of every moment,
perfectly awakened in a single moment,
bearing the own-nature of all <s>Buddhas</s>.
Of bodiless body, supreme among bodies,
the illuminator of myriads of bodies,
the displayer of all forms without exception,
<s>Ratnaketu</s> (Jewel-Banner), the great gem.

body.translated_text: Thus end the twenty-four verses on the knowledge of equality.

children.translated_text: To be awakened to by all the perfectly awakened ones,
the unsurpassed <s>Buddha-bodhi</s> (Buddha-awakening),
without syllables, the source of <s>mantras</s>,
the three families of the great <s>mantras</s>.
The generator of the meaning of all <s>mantras</s>,
the great <s>bindu</s> (drop), without syllables,
the five-syllabled one, the great void,
the void of the <s>bindu</s>, the six-syllabled one.
Of all forms, yet formless,
bearing the half-half of the sixteen <s>bindus</s>,
partless, beyond the division of parts,
bearing the summit of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation).
Knowing all the arts of all <s>dhyānas</s>,
the knower of the lineage and clan of <s>samādhi</s>,
the body of <s>samādhi</s>, supreme among bodies,
the king of all <s>saṃbhogakāyas</s> (enjoyment-bodies).
The <s>nirmāṇakāya</s> (emanation-body), supreme among bodies,
bearing the lineage of <s>Buddha</s>-emanations,
the universal emanation in the ten directions,
the accomplisher of the world's purpose as it truly is.
The god beyond gods, the lord of gods,
the lord of the celestials, the ruler of the <s>Dānavas</s>,
the lord of the immortals, the guru of the gods,
<s>Pramatha</s> (the tormentor), the lord of the <s>Pramathas</s>.
Having crossed beyond the wilderness of existence,
the sole teacher, the guru of the world,
renowned throughout the worlds of the ten directions,
the great lord of the gift of <s>Dharma</s>.
Clad in the armor of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness),
protected by the mail of <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion),
with the sword, bow, and arrow of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom),
the destroyer of the battle of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and ignorance.
The enemy of <s>Māra</s>, the conqueror of <s>Māra</s>, the hero,
the destroyer of the fear of the four <s>Māras</s>,
the vanquisher of the entire army of <s>Māra</s>,
the perfectly awakened one, the leader of the world.
Worthy of salutation, worthy of worship, worthy of homage,
and to be honored always,
most worthy of adoration, to be esteemed,
worthy of obeisance, the supreme guru.
Traversing the three worlds in a single stride,
of a stride extending to the limits of the sky,
possessed of the three knowledges, learned, pure,
possessed of the six <s>abhijñās</s> (supernatural knowledges) and the six <s>anusmṛtis</s> (recollections).
The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the great being,
transcending the world, of great supernatural power,
grounded in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom),
having attained the truth-nature of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom).
The knower of the self, the knower of others, the all,
possessed of strength, the foremost individual,
having transcended all comparisons,
the knowable, the supreme lord of knowledge.
The best lord of the gift of <s>Dharma</s>,
the teacher of the meaning of the four <s>mudrās</s> (seals),
the most worthy of worship by the beings of the worlds
who travel the three paths of liberation.
Of glory purified in the ultimate truth,
the great fortunate one of the three worlds,
the bestower of all prosperity, the glorious one,
<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the best among the glorious.

body.translated_text: Thus end the fifteen verses on the knowledge of the performance of duties.

children.translated_text: Homage to You, O foremost <s>vajra</s> of boons,
homage to You, O summit of reality,
homage to You, O womb of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness),
homage to You, O <s>Buddha-bodhi</s> (Buddha-awakening).
Homage to You, O <s>Buddha</s>-passion,
homage, homage, O <s>Buddha</s>-desire,
homage to You, O <s>Buddha</s>-delight,
homage, homage, O <s>Buddha</s>-joy.
Homage to You, O <s>Buddha</s>-smile,
homage, homage, O <s>Buddha</s>-laughter,
homage to You, O <s>Buddha</s>-speech,
homage, homage, O <s>Buddha</s>-nature.
Homage to You, O one born from non-being,
homage to You, O one born from the <s>Buddha</s>,
homage to You, O one born from the sky,
homage to You, O one born from knowledge.
Homage to You, O net of <s>māyā</s> (illusion),
homage to You, O dramatic play of the <s>Buddha</s>,
homage to You among all and for all,
homage to You, O body of knowledge.

body.text:
[...]
iyamasau vajrapāṇeḥ vajradharabhagavato jñānamūrteḥ sarvatathāgatajñānakāyasya mañjuśrījñānasattvasyāveṇikapariśuddhā nāmasaṃgitistavānuttaraprītiprāsādamahodvilya saṅjananārthahṃ, kāyavāṅmanoguhyapariśuddhyai, aparipūrṇapariśuddhabhūmiparimitāpuṇyajñānasaṃbhāraparipūripariśuddhyai, anadhigatānuttarārthasyādhigamāya, aprāptasya prāptyai, yāvatsarvatathāgatasarvadharmanetrīsaṃdhāraṇārthaṃ ca mayā deśitā, saṃprakāśitā, vivṛtā, vibhajitottānikṛtā, adhiṣṭhatā cayaṃ mayā vajrapāṇe vajradhara tava santāne citte sarvamantradharmatādhiṣṭhāneneti || Mns_163 ||
iti prathamacakrasyeyamanuśaṃsā ekādaśa padāni
body.translated_text: This is the supremely pure chanting of names (<s>Nāmasaṃgīti</s>) of the <s>Bhagavat</s> <s>Mañjuśrī-jñānasattva</s>, the knowledge-body of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the knowledge-form of the <s>Bhagavat</s> <s>Vajradhara</s> of <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, generating supreme delight and joy, for the purpose of purifying body, speech, and mind, for the complete purification of the accumulation of merit and knowledge for those who have not fulfilled the purification of the stages, for the attainment of the unattained supreme aim, for the attainment of what has not been attained, and for the comprehension of the <s>Dharma</s>-matrix of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> — thus has it been taught, proclaimed, disclosed, analyzed, made clear, and empowered by me, O <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, O <s>Vajradhara</s>, by the empowerment of the <s>Dharma</s>-nature of all <s>mantras</s> in your continuum and mind. These are the eleven words of the commendation of the first cycle.

children.translated_text: Then the glorious <s>Vajradhara</s>,
delighted and satisfied, with palms joined,
bowing to the protector, the perfectly awakened one,
the <s>Bhagavat</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>,
together with many other protectors,
lords of the secret, <s>Vajrapāṇis</s>,
along with the kings of wrath,
spoke aloud these words:
"We rejoice, O Protector!
Excellent, excellent, well spoken!
A great purpose has been accomplished for us,
one that leads to perfect awakening.
And for the world, which is without a protector,
longing for the fruit of liberation,
this is the purified path to the highest good,
proclaimed through the method of the net of <s>māyā</s>.
Profound, noble, and vast,
of great purpose, accomplishing the world's aim,
this is indeed the domain of the <s>Buddhas</s>,
spoken by the perfectly awakened one."

body.translated_text: Thus end the five concluding verses.

body.text: ārthamāyājālaṣoḍaśasāhāsrikān mahāyogatantrāntaḥ pātisamādhijālapaṭalād bhagavatā śrīśākyamuninā bhāṣitā bhagavato mañjuśrījñānasattvasyādvayaparamārtha nāmasaṃgītiḥ parisamāptā |
body.translated_text: From the chapter on the <s>Samādhijāla</s> (Net of Meditative Absorption) within the <s>Māyājālaṣoḍaśasāhasrika Mahāyogatantra</s>, this <s>Nāmasaṃgīti</s> (Chanting of Names) of the non-dual ultimate truth of the <s>Bhagavat</s> <s>Mañjuśrī-jñānasattva</s>, spoken by the <s>Bhagavat</s> <s>Śrī Śākyamuni</s>, is completed.

body.text: ī. siṅ. likhyata, jayakarta, yavadvīpa, saṃ. 1423
